policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the lemma as 'the meek,' distinguishing ketiv ענוים from qere עֲנִיִּים ('poor/needy'); the alternative-rendering note 'Or, poor' concerns English wording and does not override the ASV text.
ASV renders the lemma with the definite article as 'the fruitful field' in 'and the fruitful field be esteemed as a forest,' distinguishing qere וְהַכַּרְמֶל from ketiv וכרמל without the article.
